title: Emerging trends in molecular synthesis and synergistic intumescent engineering of bio-derived materials for fire protection
content: Advancements in bio-based materials have led to the development of sustainable flame-retardants derived from renewable resources, offering a promising alternative to conventional, petroleum-based additives. To address fire hazards and improve material safety, the integration of bio-based flame-retardants into polymer matrices has emerged as an effective strategy. These bio-based compounds, including cellulose, proteins, cardanol, phytic acid, DNA and adenosine triphosphate, exhibit unique properties that significantly enhance the flame retardancy of materials. When incorporated into polymers, these compounds form stable char layers during combustion, reducing heat and oxygen transfer and inhibiting the release of volatile combustible gases, thereby improving the flame-retardant behavior of the material. This review provides an overview of bio-based flame-retardants, emphasizing their char-forming ability and chemical interactions to enhance flame retardancy. It explores key bio-based flame-retardants, their mechanisms, and the synergistic effects of combining them with phosphorus and nitrogen-containing compounds for improved flame retardancy. The review also highlights the importance of understanding the botanical origin and extraction processes to address variability challenges and optimize industrial use. Finally, it suggests future research directions to improve scalability and compatibility for broader industrial applications of bio-based flame-retardants.
